subject: Re: Request to split 3-year prepay across fiscal years / revenue recognition
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>

Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Split invoicing for 3yr prepay - accounting ask

Marcus —

Thanks again for the proposal. Our finance team has a quick question before we sign: for a 3-year prepaid commitment, would Redwood be able to issue invoices split by fiscal year so we can match payments to our annual budget (FY26, FY27, FY28)? We prefer to pay the committed amount in the 3-year cadence you quoted, but need an invoice per fiscal year for our internal approval and rev rec.

Also, can you confirm how this impacts the term discount you gave (15% off list) — does that apply to the full 3-year sum or will it be prorated if we invoice by year?

If you can share a sample invoice schedule (line items + PO references) that would help our accounting team.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Finance
Acme Retail Systems

Attachment: Acme_PO_49821.pdf (PO stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_k@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Split invoicing for 3yr prepay - accounting ask

Looping you both in — Acme wants to pay the committed amount but receive invoices split by fiscal year (they referenced FY26-28). They also asked whether the 15% term discount applies to the full prepay or whether we need to prorate if we produce annual invoices.

Questions for finance/legal:
- Is it acceptable operationally to produce three separate invoices that total the prepay amount, with Invoice dates falling in different fiscal years?
- From rev rec perspective (ASC 606), do we need to recognize revenue on cash receipt or over time? Any customer-facing language we should include in the amendment so this doesn't create surprised audit findings for Acme?

Marissa — can you confirm any billing system constraints (SAP/Stripe exports) that would make year-split invoices difficult?

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Customer GTM, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_k@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Split invoicing for 3yr prepay - accounting ask

Marcus —

High level answer: yes, we can issue split invoices, but we need to be explicit in contract/amendment around billing milestones and revenue recognition. Quick notes: 

1) RevRec (ASC 606) 
- For a prepaid multi-year contract, revenue is generally recognized over the period services are provided (i.e., prorated over the 36 months), not fully on receipt of cash. So issuing three invoices does not by itself change revenue recognition — we still recognize over time.
- If Acme wants each invoice to correspond to a budget year, we can produce invoice documents dated in each fiscal year. We then book deferred revenue on receipt and amortize (recognize) over the service period.

2) Discount application 
- The 15% term discount that Sales approved applies to the total contracted consideration. Operationally we can apply the discount up-front to the total and reflect the net amount across the three invoices according to the agreed split. Avoid applying the discount differently across invoices unless both parties agree to a prorated schedule.

3) Accounting entries / notes for audit 
- We should provide an invoice schedule and an accounting note that states: "Total prepayment amount $X (net of 15% term discount), invoiced in 3 installments dated XX/YY/ZZ. Revenue to be recognized ratably over 36 months from contract start date." That should be sufficient for their auditors.

4) Practical/ops constraints 
- Billing: we can create three separate invoices in Stripe with separate invoice numbers and dates. Our AR process will still mark the cash receipt and post to deferred revenue; finance will perform the monthly amortization journal entries. 
- PO: make sure Acme includes a single PO referencing the master SOW and each invoice number (we can populate invoice numbers on the schedule before they submit the PO).

Suggested next step: Marcus, share a proposed invoice schedule (CSV stub) and we'll confirm the net allocation (year-by-year amounts) and the exact invoice dates so we can pre-create invoices in the system. Also, loop Legal if you want explicit amendment language.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Finance (Revenue)
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acmeretail.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_k@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Split invoicing for 3yr prepay - accounting ask

Sanjay —

Appreciate the quick question. Per our finance team (cc'd), we can absolutely produce the invoices split by fiscal year. Attached is a proposed invoice schedule and a redlined SOW that includes a short amendment clause to make the billing schedule explicit. Summary below: 

- Contract value (gross): $1,200,000 for 36 months
- Term discount: 15% applied to the full contract -> Net = $1,020,000
- Proposed invoice plan (payable to Redwood Inference):
   - Invoice #1 (FY26) dated 2026-06-30: $360,000 (covers months 1-12)
   - Invoice #2 (FY27) dated 2027-06-30: $340,000 (covers months 13-24)
   - Invoice #3 (FY28) dated 2028-06-30: $320,000 (covers months 25-36)

Notes: numbers above reflect a modest front-loaded schedule to match Acme's FY26 budget and to account for volume ramp in year 1; we can also present an equal-split option if you prefer exact yearly parity. All invoices will reference Acme PO 49821 and the master SOW. We will treat the total as a prepaid contract for rev rec; Redwood will recognize revenue ratably over 36 months.

I've attached: Redwood_SOW_3yr_v4.pdf (redline), InvoiceBreakdown_3yr.csv (CSV with invoice lines). If this looks good I can prepare an amendment and a DocuSign envelope for signatures, and pre-create the invoices so your AP can match the PO to the invoice numbers.

Next step: can you confirm which invoice dates/numbers you want on the PO and whether you want the discount applied differently across years?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer GTM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_3yr_v4.pdf, InvoiceBreakdown_3yr.csv

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>

Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Split invoicing for 3yr prepay - accounting ask

Marcus —

Thanks for the schedule and the documentation. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) PO: we've attached the PO (Acme_PO_49821.pdf) and want Invoice #1 to be dated 2026-06-30 and reference that PO. We can approve FY26 payment once invoice #1 arrives.

2) Discount: our procurement prefers the discount be reflected up front (so the three invoices show net amounts that sum to the total discounted value). That matches Neha's note — good.

3) Proration: small ask — because our FY27 headcount forecast may shift we may need to split Invoice #2 across two internal cost centers. Would Redwood be able to accept a single invoice with two distribution lines (same invoice number but two GL allocations)? Or do we need to produce two invoices for internal chargebacks?

If you can confirm the single-invoice-with-multiple-lines approach we can proceed. If everything looks good we'll sign the amendment/DocuSign you send and return the PO.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Finance
Acme Retail Systems

Attachment: Acme_PO_49821.pdf (resent)

Sanjay —

Thanks — that all works. Confirmations and next steps: 

- Discount: we will apply the 15% discount to the total contract and display net values on each invoice so the three invoices sum to $1,020,000.
- Invoice format: we can issue Invoice #2 as a single invoice with multiple distribution lines (two GL/Cost-center allocation lines) — our billing system supports line-level descriptions and cost-center tags. Please provide the GL/Cost-center codes for the two allocations and the split percentages/amounts.
- Invoice creation: Billing will pre-create the three invoice numbers and populate them in the amendment. We'll send the DocuSign envelope for signature with invoice numbers embedded so Acme's AP can match to the PO.
- RevRec: Redwood will treat payments as prepaid and recognize revenue ratably over 36 months as noted by Neha. We'll include a short accounting note in the amendment for your auditors.

Action items:
- Sanjay / Acme: reply with allocation codes for Invoice #2 and confirm you approve the dates above.
- Billing Team (cc): please pre-create three invoices in Stripe/NetSuite with the amounts in InvoiceBreakdown_3yr.csv and hold them pending DocuSign and PO match.
- Marcus/Legal: I'll route the amendment for signature once billing confirms invoice numbers.

If all good, I'll send the DocuSign link this afternoon.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer GTM, Redwood Inference
